steps_tex: Smallest: $10 \times 10 = 100$, which has $3$ digits.
Largest: $99 \times 99 = 9801$, which has $4$ digits.
Every other product lies between them, so Roxie is right.
Two $3$-digit numbers: the smallest is $100 \times 100 = 10,000$, which already has $5$ digits. So never $4$ digits.
For a $4$-digit and a $2$-digit number: the smallest is $1000 \times 10 = 10,000$, which has $5$ digits, so yes.
The largest is $9999 \times 99 = 9,89,901$, which has $6$ digits.

steps_tex: Exchanging two digits makes the number bigger only if the smaller digit is on the left.

The millionth digit is $10,00,000 - 4,88,889 = 5,11,111$ digits into the $6$-digit numbers. $5,11,111 \div 6$ gives $85,185$ whole numbers and $1$ left over. So it is the first digit of $1,00,000 + 85,185 = 1,85,185$, and the digit is $1$.
$(c)$: Counting the fives written by computer, the digit $5$ is written for the $5000\text{th}$ time in the number $13,495$.
